english: A ceiling fan has three blades whose tips $P$, $Q$, $R$ are at a distance of $0.9$ m from the axis, the angle between the lines from the axis to any two of the tips being $120^\circ$, and $Q$, $R$ follow $P$ in the anticlockwise sense. Take the axis as the origin, the $x$-axis pointing east and the $y$-axis pointing north, with distances in metres. Initially $P$ is at $(0.9,0)$. The fan turns anticlockwise until the tip $P$ has travelled a distance of $19.05\pi$ m along its circular path. Then the sum of the $y$-coordinates of those tips that lie below the $x$-axis is ______.
hindi: एक छत के पंखे की तीन पंखुड़ियों के सिरे $P$, $Q$, $R$ अक्ष से $0.9$ m की दूरी पर हैं, अक्ष से किन्हीं दो सिरों तक की रेखाओं के बीच का कोण $120^\circ$ है, तथा वामावर्त दिशा में $P$ के बाद $Q$, $R$ आते हैं। अक्ष को मूलबिन्दु, $x$-अक्ष को पूर्व की ओर तथा $y$-अक्ष को उत्तर की ओर लीजिए, दूरियाँ मीटर में हैं। प्रारम्भ में $P$ बिन्दु $(0.9,0)$ पर है। पंखा वामावर्त घूमता है जब तक सिरा $P$ अपने वृत्तीय पथ पर $19.05\pi$ m की दूरी तय नहीं कर लेता। तब $x$-अक्ष के नीचे स्थित सिरों के $y$-निर्देशांकों का योग ______ है।
solution: Angle turned $\theta=\dfrac{\ell}{r}=\dfrac{19.05\pi}{0.9}=\dfrac{127\pi}{6}=20\pi+\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$, so $P$ is at angle $\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$
Sum for the tips below the $x$-axis $=-0.45-0.45=-0.9$
solution_full: Since $\dfrac{127\pi}{6}=10(2\pi)+\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$, after ten full turns $P$ is at the angle $\dfrac{7\pi}{6}$ (that is $210^\circ$) from the positive $x$-axis.
$Q$ and $R$ are $120^\circ$ and $240^\circ$ ahead of $P$ anticlockwise: at $210^\circ+120^\circ=330^\circ$ and $210^\circ+240^\circ=450^\circ$, that is $90^\circ$.

Allied angles: $\sin 210^\circ=\sin(180^\circ+30^\circ)=-\sin 30^\circ=-\dfrac12$ (third quadrant, sine negative); $\sin 330^\circ=\sin(360^\circ-30^\circ)=-\dfrac12$ (fourth quadrant); $\sin 90^\circ=1$.
So $y_P=0.9\left(-\dfrac12\right)=-0.45$, $y_Q=-0.45$ and $y_R=0.9$. Only $P$ and $Q$ are below the $x$-axis.
originality_note: New: a rotating three-blade configuration where the arc travelled by one tip fixes the turn (127 pi/6, ten full turns plus 210 degrees) and the 120 degree offsets send the other tips into different quadrants (way 5). Closest known: position of one point on a rotating wheel or fan blade. Different because: three tips must be placed, and the quadrant of each decides whether it counts.
blueprint_concepts: Measurement of angles: degree, radian, arc length and sector area
Trigonometric ratios of allied angles; signs in the four quadrants

concept_use.Measurement of angles: degree, radian, a: theta = l/r = 127 pi/6 radian, reduced by 10 full turns to 210 degrees.
concept_use.Trigonometric ratios of allied angles; s: sin 210 = -sin 30, sin 330 = -sin 30, sin 450 = sin 90, with the quadrant deciding the sign and which tips are below the x-axis.
